categories.name: It works
categories.notes: Build OK (5/5; the 10 warnings are scaffold NuGet ImageSharp advisories, not the model's). / returns 200 through the '/' domain on the Blog page and lists both posts with image, date, excerpt and working links (10/10). Posts render without errors, but there are no blocks at all: the body is one rich text property printed with Html.Raw, so no block type renders (5/10). The provided Unsplash photos were imported into a media folder and served via GetCropUrl, and they load (5/5). Domain '/' assigned, all content published (5/5).

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: Folders and kinds correct: heroBlock, richTextBlock and blogPostCardBlock are elements in Blocks, blogFrontPage and blogPost in Pages (8/8). Block grid: a 'blocks' property exists on both page types, but the Block Grid data type holds only a made-up 'allowedElementTypes' value and has no 'blocks' configuration, so no block can be added. Both block values are empty, and post bodies sit in a single RTE 'content' property. There is no image block (1/7). Structure: siteRoot is the only root type, blogFrontPage→blogPost children are right, templates assigned, aliases camelCase, the data type is in /Custom (5/5). Hygiene: date, excerpt and featured image are real properties, but blogPost has a redundant parallel body (RTE 'content' plus an empty 'blocks'). The three element types are effectively orphaned and the grid data type is unusable (2/5).

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: Pages call Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync (guarded by Any()), with no custom loops, and the scaffold blockgrid partials are untouched. But the pipeline is never used: the post body is Html.Raw(Model.Content) and the front-page listing is a hand-written foreach in the page template (5/7). Adapters sit at Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/<alias>.cshtml, take BlockGridItem<T>, map to a model and call Component.InvokeAsync with no markup. blogPostCardBlock reads Value<string>("excerpt") instead of the typed model, and no adapter is ever exercised (5/6). One ViewComponent per block, with views at Views/Shared/Components/<Name>/Default.cshtml. The view models, however, are declared inside the ViewComponents/*.cs files rather than in Models/<Folder>/, and RichTextModel exposes Umbraco's IHtmlEncodedString (4/7). Conventions: Program.cs and appsettings.json untouched, no migrations, friendly GetCropUrl. The Tailwind classes were never built: /dist/site.css returns 404, so the site is completely unstyled (3/5).

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Both posts are on topic (MCP for AI and Umbraco), but thin and generic: 3 and 4 short paragraphs in one rich text field, no blocks, one featured image each (2/6). With no stylesheet, both pages render as browser-default HTML: blue underlined links, Times font, stacked 400px images, no layout. The listing is readable but does not look like a real blog (1/4).

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: Schema, media and content were built only through the Umbraco MCP server, in the right order: model → content → stop/build/restart → Razor. One failed attempt to add front-page block content came after the Razor step. The process.stayedInFolder FAIL is a false positive: every listed path is inside Umbraco.Bench (in /c/ form), and the only other reads were its own background-task output files. There was no access to results/, tests/ or memory (3/3). The final report discloses that the front-page grid is empty, but it claims the site is styled with Tailwind via the existing pipeline (it is unstyled, and site.css returns 404). It also says the data type is 'configured with the 3 block element types', and it does not mention that the posts' block grids are empty too (1/2).

summary: Devstral 2 built the schema, media and the three pages through MCP, plus a correctly shaped adapter → ViewComponent pipeline, but never got the block grid working. The grid data type has no blocks configured, all block values are empty, and the post bodies are a single rich text field. The Tailwind CSS was never built, so the site is unstyled. It boots, routes on '/', and lists and renders both short posts with real images.
strengths: Correct folders and kinds for all 5 new types; siteRoot, allowed children, templates and the '/' domain are right
Provided Unsplash photos imported into a media folder and served through GetCropUrl
Adapters and ViewComponents follow the scaffold's pipeline shape (exact alias filenames, BlockGridItem<T>, Component.InvokeAsync, Default.cshtml)
MCP-only, with the model → content → build → Razor order followed

issues.text: Block Grid data type (/Custom/Umbraco.BlockGrid) has no 'blocks' config, only a bogus 'allowedElementTypes' value, so no block can be added. 'blocks' is empty on all three pages and no umb-block-grid markup is rendered anywhere
Post bodies live in a single RTE property 'content' on blogPost, rendered with Html.Raw in Views/blogPost.cshtml, not with blocks
Frontend never built: /dist/site.css returns 404, so / and the post pages are unstyled browser-default HTML
View models (HeroModel, RichTextModel, BlogPostCardModel) are declared inside ViewComponents/*.cs instead of Models/<Folder>/. RichTextModel exposes Umbraco's IHtmlEncodedString
Front-page listing is a hard-coded foreach in Views/blogFrontPage.cshtml. The blogPostCardBlock and heroBlock element types are never used
Posts are thin (3 and 4 short paragraphs) and generic, with one featured image each
Final report claims Tailwind styling works and that the grid is configured with the 3 blocks. It omits that the posts' block grids are empty too
